events.title: Sun Microsystems founded
events.summary: Andy Bechtolsheim, Vinod Khosla, Bill Joy, and Scott McNealy founded Sun Microsystems on February 24, 1982 — to commercialize the Stanford University Network [workstation].
events.about: Sun bet on Unix, open networking, and [RISC] before those were industry defaults. NFS, Java, SPARC, and the slogan "the network is the computer" came from this company — shaping how servers, developers, and enterprises built distributed systems through the dot-com era.

narrative.whyChosen: Sun turned Berkeley Unix and networking research into a [workstation] empire.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved open protocols and Unix could win in commercial computing.
narrative.problemSolved: Engineers needed affordable networked Unix machines, not locked proprietary minicomputers.
